clue.text: Keep scholars in to put straight

parts.note: BAs are graduates holding a Bachelor of Arts, so scholars gives the plural BAS

indicators.note: to put something straight is to tidy it into order, so the two little words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Students are kept in after school to sort out their behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' is the castle's inner stronghold, not the verb; 'put straight' rearranges the two short words after the graduates.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the innermost fortified tower of a castle, a stronghold or bulwark.

clue.text: To rise to the occasion is better all round

indicators.note: the word for better wraps entirely round the little word is, holding it within

parts.note: to better something is to improve it

explanation.surface: Meeting a challenge on the spot is the best all-round approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all round' wraps the word for better around 'is'; the definition keeps its 'To' because it is an infinitive.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to cope with the unexpected without preparation, rising to whatever the moment demands.

clue.text: Basic security for sailing folk

parts.note: the heavy weight a ship drops to stay put is literally the sailors' security, and figuratively anything that gives basic stability

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's heavy hook holds it in place, and figuratively it is a source of stability or security.

clue.text: A worrisome fellow, a right nincompoop, in a woman's clutches

indicators.note: the fool and his companions sit inside the woman's word
being in someone's clutches means held within their grip, so her word encloses the rest

parts.note: her is the possessive pronoun for a woman
taken as written
an ass is a fool or nincompoop

explanation.surface: A tiresome man, a real idiot, has fallen into the grip of a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'clutches' work together: the woman holds the article, the abbreviation and the fool in her grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who harasses is a pest who worries and torments others persistently.

clue.text: The contest of the century!

parts.note: sounds like hype for a big sporting event, but read literally it is a conflict lasting about a hundred years, the Anglo-French war of 1337 to 1453

explanation.definitionFit: This medieval conflict between England and France ran on and off for more than a century.

clue.text: Heartless rogue seeing some changes made

indicators.note: losing its heart means the word rogue keeps only its first and last letters

parts.note: seeing is the faculty of sight, or vision

explanation.surface: A cruel scoundrel watches as certain alterations are carried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' strips OGU from rogue, leaving RE, followed by VISION.
explanation.definitionFit: A revision is an amended version of something, a set of alterations to a text or plan.

clue.text: Rent a place in Croatia

definitions.meaning: a rent is a tear or rip, as in cloth
a coastal city on the Adriatic in Croatia

explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a tear or split in fabric; Split is also a port city on Croatia's Dalmatian coast.

clue.text: Oriental giving a key back

parts.note: E is one of the musical keys
astern is the nautical word for at or towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone from the East handing a key back to its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is not a reversal signal here: it means ASTERN, the sailor's word for behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern describes things from the East, the old sense of Oriental.

clue.text: Cricketer well-known as a crime-fighter

definitions.meaning: a batsman, a player who bats in cricket, here shortened
the caped comic-book hero of Gotham City

explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer who bats can be called a batman, and the masked vigilante of Gotham is the famous comic crime-fighter.

clue.text: The author of 'Evil's Not Wrong'

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of the quoted title are put in the wrong order

parts.note: the word evil's read with its s as a letter, as in evil is
taken as written

explanation.surface: It looks like a reference to the writer of a book titled Evil's Not Wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong', part of the mock title, rearranges EVILSNOT. The apostrophe's s is a real letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelist is a writer of fiction, an author of books.

clue.text: Looked around the church and stiffened

indicators.note: the word for looked goes around the church abbreviation

parts.note: to stare is to look fixedly

explanation.surface: Someone gazed round a church and froze stiffly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts the church abbreviation inside the past tense of gazing, splitting it after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Starched fabric has been treated with starch to make it stiff, so it has been stiffened.

clue.text: Took a seat. Even that could be material

parts.note: to take a seat is to sit, past tense sat
e'en is the old poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: Someone sat down, and even that might count as substance.
explanation.walkthrough: E'EN is a poetic shortening of 'even' (as in 'e'en so').
explanation.definitionFit: Sateen is a glossy cotton fabric woven to look like satin.

clue.text: Read poetry and talk

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or read carefully
verse is writing in metre, poetry

explanation.surface: Read some poems and discuss them.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is an old verb meaning to study or pore over.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to hold a conversation, to chat with someone.

clue.text: Medical man having to establish cause of death

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
owning something is having it

explanation.surface: A doctor must determine why someone died.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a coroner's job; 'having' quietly supplies OWNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffocating in water is a common fatal accident, a frequent finding at inquests.

clue.text: His image meant everything to him —- such a bloomer!

definitions.text: His image meant everything to him
definitions.meaning: the Greek youth who fell in love with his own reflection in a pool
a bloomer here is a flowering plant, the daffodil genus

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the youth loved his own reflection; the daffodil genus bears his name as a spring flower.

clue.text: Cut the allowance for a knight

parts.note: to lance is to cut open, as a boil
a lot is a share or portion allotted to someone

explanation.surface: Someone is reducing the pay granted to a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a reduction but supplies LANCE, the surgeon's verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot was the foremost knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: Insurance too is included in the pound!

indicators.note: the word for too sits inside the word for the enclosure

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, a cage
over means too, excessively, as in over-eager

explanation.surface: An insurance policy whose excess is part of the price in pounds sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money but is an animal enclosure; 'is included in' places the word for too inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the protection an insurance policy provides, the scope of what it pays for.

clue.text: Redoubt specially built to stand out

indicators.note: something specially built is constructed to a new design, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A fortification has been purpose-built to stick out from the landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: A redoubt is a small fort; 'specially built' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to stick out or push forward in an unwelcome way, to protrude.

clue.text: Sense of purpose?

definitions.meaning: the sense of a word is what it signifies
one's purpose is what one intends, as in 'I didn't get your drift'

explanation.definitionFit: Significance is the sense of something, and intention or purpose is what someone has in mind.

clue.text: Items requiring editing, it's clear

indicators.note: text that needs editing is to be reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the contraction it's read with its letters only
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some pieces that need correcting are obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requiring editing' rearranges ITSCLEAR. 'Items' suggests newspaper pieces, which also fits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Articles are things or objects, as in articles of clothing, and also written pieces.

clue.text: Quotation making a number turn colour

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: turning the colour word round means reading it backwards

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: A quote causes a figure to change hue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses only the colour; a tender is a price quoted by a contractor bidding for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is a formal offer stating the price at which a contractor will do a job.

clue.text: Still among the finest at ice-dancing

indicators.note: among says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Even motionless, a skater remains one of the best at ice-dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' signals the run fineST AT ICe-dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means not moving, motionless, which is a sense of still.

clue.text: Lit up, being tense

definitions.meaning: lit up is slang for drunk

explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for drunk, and a rope pulled taut is tight, as are nerves under strain.

clue.text: Inform on other criminals repeatedly in prison

indicators.note: the slang word is given twice over

parts.note: to sing is underworld slang for informing to the police

explanation.surface: A grass keeps betraying his fellow crooks while behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: SING SING is a famous maximum-security jail in New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: Sing Sing is the well-known correctional facility at Ossining, New York.

clue.text: Close with a cheap sort of housing

parts.note: to bung is to stop up or close, as with a bung or stopper
low means cheap, as in low prices

explanation.surface: Near some inexpensive homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like 'near' but is the verb: to BUNG a hole is to plug it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a single-storey house, a type of dwelling.

clue.text: Horsey queen prepared to receive one

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the numeral, holding it inside
a dish that is prepared is made up, so the letters are made up anew

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A queen fond of riding is ready to welcome a guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges QUEEN as EQUNE, and 'to receive' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine means relating to horses, of the horse family.

clue.text: The person willing to have a go at the alternative

parts.note: to test something is to try it, have a go at it
taken as written
or is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone eager to try the other option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willing' is the pun: a testator is a person making a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is someone who has made a will, so the person doing the willing.
